Randle shot 52.4% from the field and 34.4% from three-point range during the 2018-19 season.
The New York Knicks finished the previous season with a 17-65 record, indicating a need for a primary scoring option.
On July 6, 2018, Trevor Ariza signed a one-year, $15 million contract with the Phoenix Suns.
On December 17, 2018, Trevor Ariza was traded to the Washington Wizards, where he averaged 14.1 points and 3.8 assists per game in 43 games.

Jeremy Lamb averaged 15.3 points per game, 5.5 rebounds per game, and 28.5 minutes per game during the 2018-19 season.
Jeremy Lamb was listed as an unrestricted free agent with a cap hold of $14,227,907 for the 2019-20 season.
Jeremy Lamb was named the starting shooting guard for the Charlotte Hornets prior to the start of the 2018-19 season.
Jeremy Lamb scored a career-high 31 points in a double-overtime game against the Brooklyn Nets on December 26, 2018.
Jeremy Lamb hit a buzzer-beater against the Toronto Raptors on March 24, 2019, which was the second-longest game-winning buzzer-beater in the previous 20 seasons.
DeAndre Jordan opted out of his $24.1 million player option for the 2018-19 season to enter free agency.
DeAndre Jordan averaged 11.0 points and 13.1 rebounds per game during the 2018-19 regular season.
DeAndre Jordan was traded to the Dallas Mavericks on the 2019 trade deadline (February 2019) as part of a package involving Kristaps Porzingis.
DeAndre Jordan was a three-time All-NBA selection and a career-high rebounder in the 2017-18 season with 15.2 rebounds per game.
In the 2015 free agency period, DeAndre Jordan re-signed with the Los Angeles Clippers on a 4-year, $80 million contract.
DeAndre Jordan will turn 30 years old in July 2019, placing him in the age range where teams typically offer shorter-term deals to centers.
On July 8, 2017, J.J. Redick signed a one-year, $23 million contract with the Philadelphia 76ers.
On July 6, 2018, J.J. Redick re-signed with the Philadelphia 76ers for a one-year contract valued at $12.25 million.
In the 2018-19 season, J.J. Redick averaged 18.1 points per game while shooting 39.7% from three-point range over 76 games.
The 2019-20 NBA salary cap was projected to be $109 million.
J.J. Redick was an official free agent in 2019 after his one-year deal with the 76ers expired.

Bojan Bogdanovic averaged 18.0 points and 4.1 rebounds per game in the 2018-19 season while shooting 49.7% from the field and 42.5% from three-point range, marking career highs in all these categories.
On June 30, 2019, it was reported that Bojan Bogdanovic agreed to a four-year, $73 million contract with the Utah Jazz.
The Indiana Pacers had previously estimated they could sign Bogdanovic to a three-year, $52-55 million deal before the Jazz entered the bidding.
The Utah Jazz initially targeted Nikola Mirotic but shifted their focus to Bogdanovic after Mirotic decided to return to Europe, leading to the Jazz offering a four-year, $73 million contract.
Bogdanovic was a restricted free agent in 2019, having declined a player option and received a qualifying offer from the Indiana Pacers.
D'Angelo Russell was named an All-Star for the 2019 season on February 1, 2019.
D'Angelo Russell averaged 21.1 points per game and 7.0 assists per game during the 2018-19 season.
The projected NBA salary cap for the 2019-20 season is $109 million.
D'Angelo Russell is eligible for a max contract starting at $27.3 million in the first season if he signs with the Nets.
The Brooklyn Nets extended a qualifying offer to D'Angelo Russell on June 28, 2019, making him a restricted free agent.
D'Angelo Russell led the Nets to the 6th seed in the Eastern Conference with a 42-40 record in the 2018-19 season.
On June 29, 2019, Shams Charania reported that Kemba Walker intends to sign with the Boston Celtics on a four-year, $141 million maximum contract.
Kemba Walker was named to the All-NBA Third Team on April 18, 2019, making him eligible for the Supermax contract (5 years, $221.3 million) if he re-signed with Charlotte.
In the 2018-19 season, Kemba Walker averaged 25.6 points, 5.9 assists, and 4.4 rebounds per game while making 260 three-pointers.
The 2019-20 NBA salary cap was projected to be $109 million, setting the maximum salary for a player with 10+ years of service at approximately $30.7 million per year.
Kemba Walker has been an All-Star three times (2016, 2017, 2018) and is entering his 10th NBA season in 2019-20.
The $141 million figure for a four-year contract results in an Average Annual Value (AAV) of $35.25 million.
Kawhi Leonard led the Toronto Raptors to the 2019 NBA Championship and was named the NBA Finals MVP for the second time in his career.
Kawhi Leonard scored 732 points during the 2019 playoffs, the third-best scoring total in a single postseason in league history.
The NBA salary cap projection for the 2019/20 season was set at $109 million.
Based on the $109 million cap projection, the maximum salary for a player with 10+ years of experience signing with a new team in the 2019/20 season was projected at $38,150,000.
Kawhi Leonard qualified for the Designated Veteran Extension (10+ years experience) prior to his trade, making him eligible for the highest maximum salary tier.
Kawhi Leonard entered the 2019 free agency period as a healthy player after playing 60 regular-season games and 24 playoff games for the Raptors.
The Los Angeles Clippers were actively recruiting Kawhi Leonard and had a roster capable of competing for a championship, positioning them as a top suitor.
Dewayne Dedmon exercised a $7.2 million player option for the 2018-19 season, indicating his current market value is anchored around that figure.
Dedmon signed with the Atlanta Hawks on July 21, 2017, to a contract that included a player option for the 2018-19 season.
During the 2018-19 season, Dedmon averaged 10.8 points, 7.5 rebounds, and 1.1 blocks per game while shooting 38.2% from three-point range.
Dedmon was ranked as having the highest defensive player impact plus/minus on the Atlanta Hawks roster at 1.2 per BBall Index during the 2018-19 season.
Dedmon's cap hold for the 2019-20 season was reported at $9.4 million, reflecting the team's valuation of his rights.
Dedmon is 29 years old entering the 2019 free agency period, which typically limits the length and value of contracts for non-star centers.
Dedmon's shooting efficiency improved significantly in 2018-19, shooting 38.2% from three-point range compared to 35.5% in the previous season.
Seth Curry signed a two-year contract with the Portland Trail Blazers on July 6, 2018, which guaranteed $2.75 million for the 2018-19 season and included a player option for the second year.
Seth Curry missed the entire 2017-18 season due to a stress reaction in his left tibia requiring surgery, with the injury diagnosed in October 2017 and surgery occurring in February 2018.
In the 2018-19 season with the Portland Trail Blazers, Seth Curry played 74 games, averaging 18.9 minutes per game and scoring 7.9 points per game while shooting 45.0% from three-point range.
Seth Curry was selected to compete in the 2019 NBA Three-Point Contest, indicating his status as a recognized elite shooter in the league.
Seth Curry's career averages prior to the 2018-19 season were 10.2 points, 2.1 rebounds, and 2.2 assists per game, with a career three-point percentage of 43.2%.

The 2019 NBA free agency market for role players and shooters was characterized by teams seeking reliable floor-spacing specialists, with similar shooters often signing for amounts between $2 million and $5 million annually depending on health history.
DeMarre Carroll agreed to a four-year, $60 million deal with the Toronto Raptors in July 2016, which was announced on July 7, 2016.
In the 2017-18 season, DeMarre Carroll played 73 games for the Brooklyn Nets, averaging 13.5 points, 6.6 rebounds, and 2.0 assists per game.
In the 2018-19 season, DeMarre Carroll played 67 games for the Brooklyn Nets, averaging 11.1 points, 5.2 rebounds, and 1.3 assists per game.
The Mid-Level Exception (MLE) for the 2017-18 season was set at $8.406 million for teams over the cap but under the luxury tax apron.
DeMarre Carroll was 30 years old as of July 2019, having turned 30 in July 2019.
DeMarre Carroll's shooting percentages declined in the 2018-19 season compared to his peak with the Hawks, shooting 39.5% from the field and 34.2% from three-point range.
A report from June 2019 indicated the Chicago Bulls were considering offering Malcolm Brogdon a 4-year, $80 million contract, which would equate to $20 million per year.
The 2019-20 NBA salary cap was projected to be $109 million, with the Bucks' luxury tax threshold at approximately $132 million.

Malcolm Brogdon was diagnosed with a plantar fascia tear in his right foot in late April 2019, with an expected recovery time of six to eight weeks, causing him to miss the remainder of the 2018-19 season.
In the 2018-19 season prior to his injury, Malcolm Brogdon started 64 games and averaged a career-high 15.6 points, 4.5 rebounds, and 3.2 assists per game.

The Milwaukee Bucks held Bird rights for Malcolm Brogdon, allowing them to exceed the salary cap to re-sign him, and were projected to have significant cap flexibility after clearing Mirza Teletovic's contract.
Brogdon was a restricted free agent in 2019, meaning the Bucks had the right to match any offer sheet he signed with another team.
The Bucks were projected to be a top-3 team in the Eastern Conference with a 52-17 record entering the 2019 playoffs, indicating Brogdon was a key contributor to a championship-contending roster.
Derrick Rose agreed to a two-year, $15 million contract with the Detroit Pistons, announced on June 27, 2019.

The 2019-20 Mid-Level Exception for teams over the salary cap was set at $9,258,000.
Derrick Rose is a three-time All-Star and the 2011 NBA MVP entering his 12th season in 2019.
Derrick Rose scored a career-high 50 points against the Utah Jazz during the 2018-19 season.
Ricky Rubio played 68 games in the 2018-19 season, averaging 12.7 points, 3.6 rebounds, 6.1 assists, and 1.3 steals per game.
Ricky Rubio's previous contract with the Utah Jazz paid him an average of approximately $14 million per year.
On June 30, 2019, it was reported that the Phoenix Suns and Ricky Rubio agreed to a three-year, $51 million contract.
Ricky Rubio had never averaged fewer than 7.3 assists per season prior to the 2017-18 season and averaged at least eight assists in five of his first six NBA seasons.
The Phoenix Suns were in need of a proven point guard to pair with Devin Booker after Booker was forced into a primary playmaking role during the 2018-19 season.
Ricky Rubio was 28 years old at the time of the 2019 free agency period.

On June 22, 2019, reports indicated the Dallas Mavericks were preparing to offer Al Horford a four-year, $112 million contract.
On June 22, 2019, reports from Marc Stein and others suggested a four-year, $112 million offer was circulating in the market for Horford.
On June 22, 2019, the NBA salary cap was projected to be approximately $109 million for the 2019-20 season, increasing the value of maximum contracts.

Marcus Morris averaged 13.9 points, 6.1 rebounds, and 1.5 assists per game during the 2018-19 regular season.

Delon Wright was acquired by the Memphis Grizzlies on February 7, 2019, in a trade involving Marc Gasol.

Delon Wright recorded three triple-doubles in his final four games of the 2018-19 regular season, including a 26-point, 14-assist, 10-rebound performance on April 5, 2019.
The 2019-20 NBA salary cap was projected to be $109 million.
Delon Wright's previous contract with the Toronto Raptors was a two-year, $3.09 million deal, with a team option of $2.54 million for the 2018-19 season.

Harrison Barnes previously signed a four-year, $94 million contract with the Dallas Mavericks in the summer of 2016.
Reports indicated that Harrison Barnes and the Sacramento Kings agreed to a four-year, $88 million contract extension.

On July 3, 2019, the Washington Wizards extended a qualifying offer to Tomas Satoransky in the amount of $3,911,484.

In the 2018-19 season, Jabari Parker averaged 14.3 points per game with the Chicago Bulls and 15.0 points per game with the Washington Wizards.

Jabari Parker suffered a second torn ACL in his left knee on February 9, 2017, with a recovery period estimated at 12 months, significantly impacting his availability and market value prior to the 2019 free agency.
The projected NBA salary cap for the 2019-20 season was $109 million.
